title: Predictive Decommission & Graceful Rebalancer for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a predictive decommissioning system paired with a graceful rebalancer to automate node lifecycle events (planned retirement, hardware failures, kernel upgrades) while preserving throughput guarantees for Dedicated capacity customers. The feature orchestrates safe drains, capacity reservations, preflight capacity checks, and live reallocation of traffic and KV caches across the fleet to minimize SLO impact. Key goals: preserve per-customer throughput SLAs during maintenance windows, support canary drains for sensitive tenants, and provide operator tooling and audit logs for each lifecycle event.
acceptance_criteria: Can schedule a predictive decommission that reserves equivalent capacity before draining starts
During a rolling decommission of up to 10% of nodes, 99th percentile latency and throughput remain within SLA for 95% of customers in a staged test
KV cache warm-transfer retains >= 90% of hot keys for migrated sessions when session-pin is enabled
Operators can pause, abort, or revert an in-flight decommission with documented runbook steps
All lifecycle events are recorded in audit logs with before/after cluster state and associated tracing IDs
implementation_notes: Controller watches node health + failure predictions (ML signal) and marks candidates for preflight capacity verification
Preflight: attempt to create temporary burst pods or reserve tokens against autoscaler to ensure headroom for rebalance
Drain phases: quarantine -> soft-drain (no new sessions) -> KV transfer -> hard-drain (evict remaining sessions)
Traffic rebalancer allocates ephemeral capacity in same region; if unavailable, fallback to model-variant routing with cost/latency penalties
Record metrics: nodes_in_decomm, drain_duration_seconds, kv_transfer_success_ratio, sla_violations_during_decomm
test_plan: Unit tests for drain state machine transitions and abort paths
Integration test: simulate predicted hardware failures and verify preflight reservations succeed
Chaos test: inject network partition during KV transfer and validate rollback semantics
Load test: 50 tenants with mixed session lengths, induce 5% node decomm and measure p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec
Canary: run on a stage Dedicated pool with two customers for 48 hours before gradual rollout
risks: Preflight reservations could fail under global peak leading to degraded SLAs if fallback isn't fast enough
KV transfer may increase network egress on metal and cause secondary hotspots
Complexity of aborting mid-KV-transfer could lead to duplicate session state unless carefully handled
Over-aggressive predictive signals risk unnecessary churn; need a conservative threshold and human-in-the-loop option

open_questions: What is the maximum acceptable KV transfer window per tenant without harming latency-sensitive workloads?
Should predictive signals be allowed to auto-schedule for low-tier customers or require manual approval?
Do we need cross-region preflight capacity reservations for geo-redundant customers?
